Lessons.Title: Arithmetic with Complex Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Determine powers of imaginary numbers and represent them on the complex plane. Determine the result of adding complex numbers, and represent it in the form $a+bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers. Use the complex plane to visualize why the sum of two complex numbers is another complex number.
Sum real and imaginary components separately. Powers i,i²=-1,i³=-i,i⁴=1 cycle with period four.

Source activity 12.1: Math Talk: Telescoping Sums: Find the value of these expressions mentally. \(2 - 2 + 20 - 20 + 200 - 200\) \(100 - 50 + 10 - 10 + 50 - 100\) \(3 + 2 + 1 + 0 - 1 - 2 - 3\) \(1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 - 16 - 8 - 4 - 2 - 1\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 12.2: Adding Complex Numbers: How do you see \(2 + 3i\) represented? How do you see \(\text- 8 - 8i\) represented? What complex number does \(A\) represent? Add “like terms” in the expression \((2 + 3i) + (\text- 8 - 8i)\). What do you get? This diagram represents \((2 + 3i) + (\text- 8 - 8i)\). \((\text- 3 + 2i) + (4 - 5i)\) (Check your work by drawing a diagram.) \((\text- 37 - 45i) + (11 + 81i)\)… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 12.3: Multiplication on the Complex Plane: Draw points to represent 2, 22, 23, and 24 on the real number line. Write \(2i\), \((2i)^2\), \((2i)^3\), and \((2i)^4\) in the form \(a+bi\). Plot \(2i\), \((2i)^2\), \((2i)^3\), and \((2i)^4\) on the complex plane. If \(a\) and \(b\) are positive numbers, is it true that \(\sqrt{ab}=\sqrt{a}\sqrt{b}\)? Explain how you know. If \(a\) and \(b\) are negative numbers, is it true… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Write each expression in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. You may plot the numbers in the complex plane as a guide. \(2 \boldcdot \sqrt{\text-4}\) \(3i \boldcdot 2i\) \(4 - 3\sqrt{\text-1}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: Which expression is equivalent to \((3+9i) - (5-3i)\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: What are \(a\) and \(b\) when you write \(\sqrt{\text-16}\) in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers? \(a=0\), \(b=\text-4\) \(a=\text-4\), \(b=0\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Fill in the boxes to make a true statement: \(\displaystyle (\boxed{\phantom{30}}-3i) - (15+\boxed{\phantom{30}}i) = 7 - 12i\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Plot each number on the real number line, or explain why the number is not on the real number line. \(\text- \sqrt{16}\) \(\sqrt{\text-16}\) \(\text- 56^{1/2}\) \((\text-56)^{1/2}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{\text-4}\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Evaluate i^7. Expected reasoning or answer: -i.
